distilled_summary: When a completed Rock workflow action must be retested, prefer a new test workflow. If an existing marked test instance must be reused, treat activation as field-based: a workflow is active when ActivatedDateTime is populated and CompletedDateTime is null; an activity also requires an active activity type, a populated ActivatedDateTime, and a null CompletedDateTime; an action is active when its CompletedDateTime is null. The workflow Status label is not the activation gate. Preflight the exact recipient, action criteria, current template, processing state, action order, and baseline side-effect counts. In Workflow Detail, leave every earlier setter, record-creation action, and unrelated communication complete; reopen only the target action, the containing activity, the workflow, and—only when reviewed and intended—a later action that closes the activity. Preserve activation and prior processed timestamps, then save once. Workflow Detail persists those changes and calls workflow processing; Rock orders active activities and actions by their configured order and skips completed actions. Verify that only the intentionally reopened action timestamps advanced, the workflow and activity re-completed, exactly one intended communication was recorded, rendered content and recipients match the approved source, and no unrelated records changed. A send cannot be rolled back: if processing is delayed or fails, inspect workflow logs and communication history before any retry, and never broadly reset workflow rows or use direct SQL updates for this operation.
reviewer_notes: Sanitized from an organization-owned operational runbook and cross-checked against the cited public Rock source. Instance identifiers, recipient data, and message content were omitted.
title: Safely retest one completed workflow action
